senses.gloss: pr. n. pl.N’hard’ʿa, Nehardea (Wood-River), 1) a place in the Arabian desert. (Wood-River),
a place in the Arabian desert.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 2:26">Targ. Y. Deut. II, 26</cite>.—2) a town in Babylonia, renowned as the seat of a college founded by Samuel.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 17b:5">Snh. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>דייני דנ׳ וכ׳</he> by ‘the judges of N.’ is meant &c.; <he>אמוראי דנ׳ וכ׳</he> by ‘the Amoraim of N.’ is meant &c.; a. fr.—Denom.
